name: Profound RF
lead: Profound is a radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system used in aesthetic clinics. It combines needle insertion into the skin with RF energy delivered at depth, and is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a hardmaxxing (clinic-based) option for skin laxity, wrinkles and acne scarring. Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure in which sterile needles repeatedly puncture the skin to induce a healing response, also called collagen induction therapy [1].

The appearance chain people describe is remodelling: needles create controlled micro-injuries, RF heat in the deeper tissue adds a tightening and collagen-stimulating effect, and over weeks to months the skin looks firmer and smoother, with scars looking shallower. The registered studies on Profound cover the sort of concerns patients seek treatment for: cellulite, wrinkles, acne scars, skin laxity and facial skin condition [2][3][4].

Evidence specific to Profound consists mainly of registered device studies on ClinicalTrials.gov, including a cellulite cartridge study, a wrinkle and acne-scar usability study and a 500-person feasibility study of the Profound Matrix system [2][3][4]. Outcome data from these registrations are not reported in the entries themselves.
infobox: Skin laxity, wrinkles, acne scars, cellulite (per registered studies)

paras: Radiofrequency microneedling adds RF energy to the mechanical injury of needling, with the stated aim of tightening and remodelling tissue beneath the skin surface. Wikipedia's article on microneedling covers the general technique, which it calls collagen induction therapy, also known as dermarolling or skin needling, and notes research is ongoing for scarring and acne [1]. It does not discuss RF devices or specific brands [1].

Wikipedia notes that some studies suggest microneedling combined with minoxidil works better than minoxidil alone for hair loss, and that the efficacy of platelet-rich plasma combinations remains in question pending further study [1]. It also reports an April 2024 CDC report of three HIV diagnoses among patients of an Albuquerque spa that offered PRP 'vampire facials', after New Mexico health officials warned about infection control in non-medical settings [1]. These concern manual microneedling and PRP, not Profound specifically.

ClinicalTrials.gov lists several Profound studies. A completed 2017 study with 31 participants evaluated Profound dermal and subcutaneous cartridges for cellulite [2]. A completed 2020 usability and feasibility study of the Profound Matrix system enrolled 193 people with wrinkles and mixed atrophic and hypertrophic acne scars [3]. A larger feasibility study of safety and performance began in 2022 with 500 participants and is listed as active, not recruiting, covering skin laxity and wrinkles [4]. A 2024 radiofrequency microneedling device study with six healthy participants was terminated [5].
These registry entries describe study designs and status; outcome data are not reported in them.
Profound is mentioned as part of the hardmaxxing category of clinic procedures for skin tightening and scar revision. No forum material with specific claims is documented here.

timeline.event: Study of Profound cartridges for cellulite begins [2].
A six-person RF microneedling device study begins and is terminated [5].

card.summary: Clinic-based radiofrequency microneedling system aimed at skin laxity, wrinkles and scars; documented mainly in registered device studies.

quick.overview:
Profound is a radiofrequency microneedling system performed in clinics. It is discussed as a way to address skin laxity, wrinkles and acne scars.
The available documentation is mostly trial registrations, including cellulite, wrinkle and acne-scar studies; outcome data are not covered here.
quick.mechanism: Microneedling punctures the skin with fine needles to trigger a healing response; RF devices add energy delivered through or beside the needles.
quick.risks: General microneedling concerns include infection risk when performed in unregulated settings, as reported by health officials in relation to related facial procedures. Device-specific safety findings are not summarized here.

chain: RF energy heats deeper skin layers
Collagen remodelling over weeks to months
Firmer, smoother skin and shallower scars
angle.text: A clinician passes the handpiece over the face or body so the needles deliver RF heat at depth. People seek it for skin tightening and for smoothing wrinkles and acne scars.
